hook: Detect blinks faster with linear attention transformers

slides.title: Eye Blink Detection for Safety and Security

bullets.text: Detecting eye blinks solves facial analysis tasks like deep fake detection and driver drowsiness monitoring.
Methods are categorized into feature-based, appearance-based, and motion-based approaches.
The approach is evaluated on blink presence detection and eye state recognition tasks using multiple public benchmark datasets.

slides.title: Challenges in Handling Noisy Data and Short Blinks

bullets.text: Existing face recognition and frame-wise classification methods struggle with short blinks or noisy data.
The CEW dataset lacks pre-defined splits, requiring a 10-fold cross-validation scheme to measure performance.
Extreme head pose angles cause most errors due to eyelid visibility and landmark precision issues.

slides.title: BlinkLinMulT: Linear Attention for Multi-Modal Input

bullets.text: Modified multi-modal transformer with linear attention considers RGB texture, landmarks, and head pose angles.
Cross-modal transformers translate between landmark features and RGB texture embeddings.
Linear multimodal transformer estimates blinks for each eye independently using backbone CNN features.

slides.title: Superior F1 Scores on RT-BENEimg and TalkingFace

bullets.text: ResNet50 achieved a 0.912 F1 score on RT-BENEimg, outperforming DenseNet121's 0.883 by a considerable margin.
Training on the union of datasets improved F1 scores: CEW rose to 0.997, ZJU to 0.933, and RT-BENEimg to 0.913.
The BlinkLinMulT model achieved a perfect 1.0 F1 score on the TalkingFace dataset for blink presence detection.
